sections.h2: What shapes the Killeen housing market?
sections.html:
Killeen sits right outside the East Gate of Fort Hood, and the post's soldiers and families drive much of the demand for houses and rentals. The city's own newcomer page for the installation links to local resources, transit and parks.

That connection means military moves, deployments and orders affect timing. Anyone with a permanent change of station order cares most about a firm closing date, and an as-is sale can deliver one.

sections.h2: What is downtown Killeen, and do special rules apply there?
sections.html:
Downtown Killeen runs from Rancier Avenue (FM 439) on the north to Veterans Memorial Boulevard (Business 190) on the south, and it is on the National Register.

If your property is empty and lies in the Historic Overlay District, the city requires you to register it and pay an annual fee. Phone Development Services before listing; buyers will ask whether the registration is current.

sections.h2: Who runs Killeen, and where do I go for a permit?
sections.html:
The 1949 city charter set up a council-manager system. A mayor and seven council members set policy, with four members elected by district and the rest at large, and elections held each May.

Permits and code questions go through city Development Services, while the appraisal side sits with the county. The city's home page also notes its adopted rate for the fiscal year that runs October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027: 73.01 cents, with the notice saying the rate raises maintenance and operations taxes compared with the prior year's rate. Read the notice in full for what that means on your bill.

sections.h2: Who sets Killeen property tax values and bills?
sections.html:
Bell Central Appraisal District sets values for Killeen in Bell County, and the city and other units set rates. Bell CAD accepts payment at its offices with no fee for check, cash or money order, while its online and phone options go through a vendor that charges fees.

It also lists a quarterly installment agreement, a homestead delinquent-tax installment agreement and a tax deferral option. Its home page notes that homestead assessed value increases of up to 10 percent a year are mandatory under the Property Tax Code until assessed value matches market value.

sections.h2: What exemptions does Bell CAD list?
sections.html:
Bell CAD lists several exemptions, and military households should look at the veteran items in particular.

  • Residence homestead
  • Disabled person and age 65 or older, including surviving spouses
  • 100 percent disabled veteran or surviving spouse
  • Surviving spouse of a service member killed in action or of a first responder killed on duty
  • Donated residence of a partially disabled veteran

It asks for a current driver license or Texas ID, a Social Security letter for disability, and a recent VA award letter for veterans. No annual renewal is needed, though the chief appraiser may request updated applications. When you sell, the buyer applies for their own exemption.

sections.h2: How do Texas tax dates apply to a Killeen sale?
sections.html:
The January 1 value and lien date, the October bills and the February 1 delinquency date set the rhythm of a Killeen closing.

  • Bell CAD notes a discount deadline of October 31 for entities that offer one.
  • A split bill has halves due at the end of November and in June.
  • The protest deadline is generally May 15.

These are state-level dates per the Comptroller, and individual taxing units may offer discounts. The county can give you the numbers for your parcel.

sections.h2: What options do I have if I must sell fast in Killeen?
sections.html:
Orders or a deployment push many Killeen owners to move fast. Three routes are open.

  • An agent listing suits a house in showing shape and an owner without a deadline.
  • Skipping the agent keeps the commission and leaves buyer management to you.
  • A cash offer takes the house unrepaired and sets the closing date with you, which suits a PCS move, a rental with problem tenants or an inherited house.

If you rent the house out from another duty station, remember the tenant side has its own court process.

sections.h2: What if squatters or an unwanted occupant are in my Killeen house?
sections.html:
Texas Property Code chapter 24B lets an owner ask the sheriff or constable for removal without a court case. The occupant must have stayed after being told to go, the property must not have been open to the public when they entered, no suit may be pending between you, and the occupant cannot be family or a current or former tenant. A removal later found wrongful can bring a lawsuit against the person who asked for it.

A real tenant is different and needs an eviction suit. Adverse possession is another idea: it means an open, hostile claim to land, with a ten-year period in the usual case. A vacant Killeen rental invites trouble, so check on it often.

sections.h2: How does a Killeen landlord sell a rental with a tenant?
sections.html:
You can sell with the lease intact or end the tenancy as the lease allows. For unpaid rent Texas requires a written notice to vacate, and the suit is filed in justice court. The tenant is served several days before trial, and either side has only five days to appeal to county court.

Once judgment is final, the writ of possession waits a few days and is then followed by a 24-hour warning. Federal notice rules may add time on some covered properties. A cash buyer may take the house with renters still inside, so you skip the court calendar.

sections.h2: What does Killeen's Fort Hood link mean for the tax and veteran side?
sections.html:
The city's newcomer page for the installation points to community services, boards and commissions, parks and a local transit service called The HOP. For a seller in a military household, Bell CAD's veteran exemptions are worth knowing about, since the donated residence of a partially disabled veteran and the surviving-spouse items are named on its page.

Texas also lets disabled veterans apply late in some cases, and Bell CAD says that if you file after April 30 you should still submit an application so the office can apply any remedy the law provides once it approves it. Gather a recent VA award letter before you call.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded, and what about probate or foreclosure?
sections.html:
The Bell County clerk records deeds for land in the county once a notary has acknowledged the signature, and the title company files at closing.

If the loan is behind, Texas runs the foreclosure outside court: a default letter, a short cure window, a courthouse notice and a first-Tuesday auction. If the owner has died, a will normally goes to probate within a few years of the death, and a small estate affidavit is only for modest estates without much real property. Get legal advice before relying on an affidavit.

faqs.a: It runs between Rancier Avenue (FM 439) and Veterans Memorial Boulevard (Business 190), just outside Fort Hood's East Gate.

faqs.q: Is there a vacant house registration in Killeen?
faqs.a: Yes, for vacant structures inside the Historic Overlay District. A 2020 ordinance requires registration with Planning and Development Services and an annual fee.

faqs.q: What is Killeen's current tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's home page announces a 73.01 cent rate for the fiscal year October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027, shown as adopted. Check the full notice and your tax statement for your own figure.

faqs.q: Does Bell CAD offer payment plans?
faqs.a: Yes. Its site lists a quarterly installment agreement, a homestead delinquent-tax installment agreement and a deferral option. Ask the office which applies.

faqs.q: Can a military household sell quickly in Killeen?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers can set the closing date around orders. A traditional listing takes longer but can bring a higher price with a house in good condition.
